title: [HTTP/2] Http2Options.MaxFrameSize and MaxConcurrentStreams are documented as advertised in SETTINGS but never sent as configured
body:
## Summary
Http2Settings.SerializeClientSettings writes four settings, hard-codes MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS to 100 and never writes SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE. Http2Options documents both options as advertised in the initial SETTINGS frame, so setting them has no effect on the wire, while a raised MaxFrameSize still widens the inbound frame bound the peer was never told about. Users who tune these options get silently different behaviour from what the docs promise.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2Settings.cs:102`

## Problem
Http2Settings.SerializeClientSettings (Http2Settings.cs:102-125) writes exactly four settings: ENABLE_PUSH, MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS hard-coded to 100 (line 107), INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE and MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE. SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE is never serialised, and the MaxConcurrentStreams property copied from the options (line 33) is never read. Http2Options documents both as 'Advertised ... in the initial SETTINGS frame' (Runtime/Core/Http2Options.cs:41-53, 86-99). The local MaxFrameSize is still used: as the inbound frame bound (Http2Connection.ReadLoop.cs:39), in the per-stream buffer size (Http2Connection.cs:182-186) and in HeaderBlockByteLimit (ReadLoop.cs:566-567). Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2SettingsTests.cs:17-41 asserts a 24-byte, four-setting payload, i.e. it pins the missing MAX_FRAME_SIZE; no test sets Http2Options.MaxFrameSize or MaxConcurrentStreams. Documentation~/Modules/Transport.md:63 shows 'options.Http2.MaxConcurrentStreams = 50' as the HTTP/2 tuning example.

**Failure scenario.** A user sets Http2.MaxFrameSize = 1 MiB to raise download throughput (#406): the server is never told, keeps sending 16,384-byte frames, and the only effects are a larger per-stream buffer budget and a client that now accepts frames up to 1 MiB that the peer was never allowed to send (RFC 9113 Section 4.2 requires FRAME_SIZE_ERROR above the advertised size). A user who follows the docs and sets MaxConcurrentStreams = 50 (or 0) changes nothing on the wire: 100 is always advertised.

## Spec reference
RFC 9113 Sections 4.2, 6.5.2

## Suggested fix
Serialise MAX_FRAME_SIZE when it differs from 16,384 and MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS from the option, or remove both options. Keep the inbound bound at 16,384 until the peer has acknowledged the larger value. Replace the docs example, and make the settings test assert the configured values.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The initial SETTINGS frame carries MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS from Http2Options and MAX_FRAME_SIZE when it differs from 16,384, or both options are removed and the docs updated
- [ ] The inbound frame bound stays at 16,384 until the peer has acknowledged a larger MAX_FRAME_SIZE (RFC 9113 section 4.2)
- [ ] The documentation example in Http2Options is corrected
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it and asserts the configured values on the wire

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http2-design-04` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http2.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: code-smell.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. SerializeClientSettings writes four settings with MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS hard-coded to 100 and no MAX_FRAME_SIZE (Http2Settings.cs:102-125); the MaxConcurrentStreams copied from options (Http2Settings.cs:33) is never read on the local side (all readers use _remoteSettings: Admission.cs:72, Http2Connection.cs:351). The local MaxFrameSize is still used as the inbound frame bound (ReadLoop.cs:39), in the per-stream buffer size (Http2Connection.cs:182-186) and HeaderBlockByteLimit (ReadLoop.cs:566-567), so raising it only loosens what the client accepts. Http2Options documents both as 'Advertised ... in the initial SETTINGS frame' (Http2Options.cs:41-53, 86-99) and Documentation~/Modules/Transport.md:63 uses MaxConcurrentStreams = 50 as the tuning example. Http2SettingsTests.cs:17-41 pins the 24-byte, four-setting payload; no test sets either option. For a client that rejects push, the MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS part is cosmetic; the MAX_FRAME_SIZE part makes a public option a no-op on the wire. #406 (download throughput) does not track it.

Also reported as `http2-protocol-07`, `http2-runtime-27` (merged into this issue).

Related: #406.

title: [HTTP/2] Fail/Cancel on another thread races TryStartResponse, so the handler gets OnResponseStart with a body source that is never terminated
body:
## Summary
Http2Stream.TryStartResponse publishes the body source and queues the handler without checking whether Cancel or Fail already completed the dispatch, and Cancel/Fail do a check-then-act on the same state without a shared lock. A deadline that fires while HEADERS is being applied can complete the request with a timeout and still deliver OnResponseStart for the same handler with an orphaned body. Callers see both an error and a response start, and a retry may replay the request.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2Stream.cs:254`

## Problem
The read loop looks the stream up and leases it (ReadLoop.cs:532), validates the header list, then calls TryStartResponse (ReadLoop.cs:740), which publishes ResponseBodySource and queues the handler (Http2Stream.cs:272-288) without checking _completionSignaled/_responseErrorQueued. Off-loop callers do check-then-act on the same state with no common lock: Cancel (522-541) and Fail (566-607) read ResponseBodySource, find null, and call TrySetException or queue OnResponseError. Callers off the loop: HandleRequestCancellation (Lifecycle.cs:202-222, request token or deadline), FailAllStreams from Dispose, PING timeout (Liveness.cs:223), write failure (Send.cs:98), send stall (Lifecycle.cs:508). The mirrored race is handled only on the error side (CompleteWithResponseStartFailure claims _completionSignaled, 704-709); InvokeResponseStartAsync (644-656) claims nothing before calling the handler. The stream was already removed from _activeStreams by the failing path, so the new body source is never completed or faulted.

**Failure scenario.** A request deadline fires while the response HEADERS frame is being applied (timeouts tend to coincide with late responses). Cancel sees no body source and completes the dispatch with OCE, mapped to Timeout and reported through OnResponseError (RawSocketTransport.cs:178-181); microseconds later the read loop queues OnResponseStartAsync for the same handler with an orphaned body. With FailAllStreams (connection failed) the retryable marker may also replay the request, so the handler sees OnResponseStart twice. The orphaned handler then runs into finding 01.

## Suggested fix
Make the first outcome one atomic state on the stream (none -> response started | failed/cancelled) claimed with CompareExchange by TryStartResponse and by Fail/Cancel; a Fail/Cancel that loses must fault the published body source, and TryStartResponse that loses must not queue the handler.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The first outcome on an Http2Stream (response started, or failed/cancelled) is claimed atomically; the losing side acts accordingly
- [ ] A Fail/Cancel that loses faults the published body source; a TryStartResponse that loses does not queue the handler
- [ ] A handler never receives both OnResponseStart and OnResponseError for one attempt
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it that forces the interleaving without sleeps

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http2-runtime-03` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http2.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: concurrency.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: No common lock or CAS covers the two sides. Read loop: CompleteHeaderBlock leases the stream (ReadLoop.cs:532) and ApplyDecodedHeaders ends in stream.TryStartResponse (740), which only checks ResponseBodySource==null and _disposed, publishes the body source and queues the handler (Http2Stream.cs:254-288) without looking at _completionSignaled/_responseErrorQueued. Off loop: HandleRequestCancellation removes the stream and calls Cancel (Lifecycle.cs:202-222); Cancel reads ResponseBodySource, sees null and calls TrySetException(OCE) (Http2Stream.cs:532-541); Fail does the same check-then-act (579-606). If Cancel's read precedes the publish at Http2Stream.cs:272, the dispatch ends with OCE -> Timeout -> OnResponseError (RawSocketTransport.cs:178-181) while InvokeResponseStartAsync still delivers OnResponseStartAsync with a body source that no path can complete or fault (stream already out of the active map, registration released). Only CompleteWithResponseStartFailure claims _completionSignaled before calling the handler (704-709). Partial mitigation: if OnResponseError arrives first, HandlerCallbackSafetyWrapper aborts the late body (HandlerCallbackSafetyWrapper.cs:48-52); in the other order the collector's body read stays parked and inner handlers see both callbacks. The window is the HEADERS-processing time after the lookup (HPACK list checks), so it is narrow but real at deadline expiry; the double OnResponseStart via replay needs an off-loop FailAllStreams in the same window.

title: [HTTP/2] DATA frames on HEAD, 204 and 304 responses are delivered to the handler as a response body
body:
## Summary
TryStartResponse only disables the content-length comparison for HEAD, 204 and 304 responses, and HandleDataFrameAsync still appends any DATA payload to the body source. RFC 9110 section 6.4.1 defines these responses as having no content, and other HTTP/2 implementations treat DATA on them as a stream error. A server or intermediary can make a cache revalidation see a 304 with a body or make a HEAD probe buffer arbitrary data.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2Stream.cs:269`

## Problem
TryStartResponse sets _expectedResponseBodyLength to -1 for IsNoContentResponse (HEAD, 204, 304) (Http2Stream.cs:269-271, 296-300), which only disables the content-length comparison; HandleDataFrameAsync then appends any DATA payload to the body source (Http2Connection.ReadLoop.cs:273-298). RFC 9110 6.4.1 defines these responses as having no content; RFC 9113 8.1.1 allows a non-zero content-length on them only 'even though no content is included in DATA frames'. The HTTP/1.1 path cannot deliver such a body because framing ends at the header section.

**Failure scenario.** A server or intermediary answers a HEAD or a conditional GET (304) with HEADERS followed by DATA: the bytes are handed to the handler chain as the body of a HEAD/304 response, e.g. a cache revalidation receives a 304 with a body, or a HEAD probe buffers an arbitrary payload up to the buffered-body cap. nghttp2 and browsers treat this as a stream PROTOCOL_ERROR.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 Section 6.4.1; RFC 9113 Section 8.1.1

## Suggested fix
For IsNoContentResponse set the expected DATA total to 0 (independent of any content-length) so the existing 'DATA exceeds content-length' path resets the stream as malformed on the first non-empty DATA frame.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A non-empty DATA frame on a HEAD, 204 or 304 response resets the stream as malformed (PROTOCOL_ERROR) and no bytes reach the handler
- [ ] A content-length header on such a response is still accepted without DATA (RFC 9113 section 8.1.1)
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http2-protocol-14` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http2.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: rfc-compat.

title: [HTTP/2] Exception mappers, timeout factory and wire literals are duplicated between the HTTP/2 types and RawSocketTransport
body:
## Summary
The request-timeout error is built twice with the same message and the wrap-as-NetworkError mapping exists three times, next to a separate handler-exception mapper. The User-Agent product token and trailer-declaration builder are also copied. A change made in one copy makes HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 report different errors or identify themselves differently.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2Stream.cs:557`

## Problem
The request-timeout error is built twice with the same message literal: Http2Stream.CreateResponseBodyCancellation (Http2Stream.cs:555-561) and RawSocketTransport.CreateRequestTimeout (RawSocketTransport.cs:832-836). 'Wrap as UHttpException(NetworkError)' exists three times: Http2Connection.MapException (Http2Connection.cs:545-547), RawSocketTransport.MapException (RawSocketTransport.cs:190-192) and Http2Stream.NormalizeTransportException (Http2Stream.cs:751-769), next to MapHandlerException, which maps to Unknown (Http2Stream.cs:739-749). The default User-Agent 'TurboHTTP/1.0' is a literal in both protocol paths (Http2Connection.cs:407-408; Http11RequestSerializer.cs:355-356). The declared-trailer header value is assembled twice (Http2Connection.cs:639-667; Http11RequestSerializer.cs:462-479). Two monotonic-clock conversions coexist (Http2MonotonicClock.cs and ToStopwatchTicks at Http2Connection.Liveness.cs:121-122).

**Failure scenario.** A change to the timeout wording, the error type of a mapped failure or the product token in User-Agent is made in one copy; HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 requests then report different errors or identify themselves differently.

## Suggested fix
Move the mappers, the timeout factory, the User-Agent constant and the trailer-declaration builder into Transport.Internal and call them from both paths.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The mappers, timeout factory, User-Agent constant and trailer-declaration builder live once in Transport.Internal and both protocol paths call them
- [ ] No duplicate copies remain in Http2Connection, Http2Stream or RawSocketTransport

title: [HTTP/2] Response-start work item signals a pooled Http2Stream after releasing its reference, so a late signal poisons the next request that rents it
body:
## Summary
InvokeResponseStartAsync drops its lifetime reference while the handler is pending and then calls TrySetResult, TrySetException or bodySource.Abort() on the stream. If the dispatch has already released its reference, the stream is back in the pool, and Initialize does not reset the completion source. The late signal then completes or aborts an unrelated request that rented the same object.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2Stream.cs:661`

## Problem
InvokeResponseStartAsync releases its reference as soon as the handler task is pending (Http2Stream.cs:657-663, 'kept alive by the dispatch and the body source') and touches the stream after the await: TrySetResult (667) or _handlerFaulted/AbortRequestBody/bodySource.Abort()/TrySetException (671-681). The dispatch reference is not guaranteed: DispatchAsync leaves through its finally (Http2Connection.cs:513-525) without awaiting CompletionTask whenever the upload phase throws after the response started (SendDataAsync at Http2Connection.cs:445: OCE from _writeLock.WaitAsync(ct) at Send.cs:189 or WaitForSendWindowAsync at Send.cs:519, or a request-body source error). bodySource.Abort() runs CleanupAsync synchronously and its finally releases the body-source reference (Http2ResponseBodySource.cs:461-464); the count reaches 0, ReleaseLifetime returns the stream to the static LIFO pool (Http2Stream.cs:805-813) and PrepareForPool zeroes _completionSignaled and resets the source (238-243). The TrySetException that follows then wins the Exchange (791) and completes the freshly reset source. Initialize (168-209) resets _completionSignaled but never calls _completionSource.Reset(), so the next Rent returns a stream whose CompletionTask is already completed. No test covers a dispatch that leaves through the upload path while the handler is still pending (the RequestTimeout tests use a streaming handler that has already completed).

**Failure scenario.** Buffered POST; the server sends response HEADERS before the upload ends, the upload is blocked on flow control, the request deadline fires. The cancel callback faults the body; the uploader throws OCE and DispatchAsync releases its reference; on another pool thread the handler's body read fails, the catch in InvokeResponseStartAsync calls bodySource.Abort() (count 0, stream pooled) and then TrySetException(HandlerCallbackException). The next HTTP/2 request in the process rents that object, sends HEADERS, and 'await stream.CompletionTask' (Http2Connection.cs:584) throws the previous request's exception immediately (or returns success with no response when the stale signal was TrySetResult); its stream leaves the active map without RST_STREAM. If the object was already re-rented, the late AbortRequestBody/TrySetException hit the live request directly.

## Suggested fix
Hold the work item's reference until InvokeResponseStartAsync has signaled completion (release only in finally, and signal before aborting the body source). Reset the completion source in Initialize and tie late signals to a rental generation so a stale work item can never complete another rental.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The work item holds its stream reference until completion has been signalled (released only in finally, signal before aborting the body source)
- [ ] Initialize resets the completion source and late signals are tied to a rental generation so a stale work item cannot complete another rental
- [ ] A request cancelled after its response started (upload blocked on flow control) never affects the next request on the pooled stream
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it that reproduces the late signal deterministically

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http2-runtime-01` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http2.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: high. Angle: concurrency.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced end to end. References: Initialize sets 1 (dispatch), TryStartResponse adds body-source and work-item refs (Http2Stream.cs:272, 286). InvokeResponseStartAsync drops the work-item ref when the handler is pending (657-663) and afterwards calls TrySetResult (667) or, in the catch, bodySource.Abort() then TrySetException (671-681). DispatchAsync releases its ref in finally without awaiting CompletionTask when the upload phase throws after the response started (Http2Connection.cs:445 -> 513-525; e.g. OCE from Send.cs:189/519 on the deadline, or a request-body error). Then the body-source ref is the last one: Abort -> BeginCleanup -> CleanupAsync runs synchronously (AbortStreamFromBodySourceAsync returns at once because the stream was already removed) and its finally calls ReleaseBodySourceLifetime (Http2ResponseBodySource.cs:461-464) -> count 0 -> Http2StreamPool.Return -> PrepareForPool zeroes _completionSignaled and resets the source (Http2Stream.cs:238-243). The following TrySetException/TrySetResult wins the Exchange (773/791) and completes the reset source of a pooled object; neither checks _disposed. Initialize (168-209) resets _completionSignaled but never _completionSource, so the next Rent from the static LIFO pool gets an already-completed CompletionTask: `await stream.CompletionTask` (Http2Connection.cs:584) returns/throws immediately for an unrelated request, which then leaves the active map without RST_STREAM (finally at 520-521). The same happens through HandlerCallbackSafetyWrapper, which aborts the body (TryAbort) before the pending callback completes. The ordering is a race between two thread-pool continuations after the deadline (uploader wake vs body-reader fault; both sources run continuations asynchronously, SingleReaderChannel.cs:288), and is deterministic when the handler is not parked in a body read. No test covers a dispatch leaving through the upload while the handler is pending.

title: [HTTP/2] Pooling Http2Stream saves one small object per request but adds a reference-count and lease protocol on every frame
body:
## Summary
Http2StreamPool keeps up to 128 pooled streams of about 200 bytes, while each response still allocates the body source, channel, header object and several other objects. Making pooling safe required reference counts, leases and identity checks on every frame path. Any new lookup without a lease or a lease held across an await can mutate another request's stream, a failure that only shows under load.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2StreamPool.cs:18`

## Problem
Http2StreamPool is a process-wide static ObjectPool of 128 streams ('~200 bytes' each, Http2StreamPool.cs:12-21). Each response still allocates an Http2ResponseBodySource with a SingleReaderChannel, its PendingReadSource, two lock objects and a TaskCompletionSource<HttpHeaders> (Http2Stream.cs:272; Http2ResponseBodySource.cs:35-39, 64), an HttpHeaders, and often an expect-continue TaskCompletionSource; the stream itself carries a lock object (Http2Stream.cs:63). To make reuse safe the stream has a lifetime count with four kinds of holders (dispatch, body source, queued start/error work item, lookup lease: Http2Stream.cs:274, 287, 352-374, 606, 805-813), every read-loop frame and every scan goes through TryAcquireLease with an identity re-check (ReadLoop.cs:364-371, 872; Lifecycle.cs:187-200, 476), and callbacks guard against a recycled instance (_disposed checks in Fail/Cancel/HandleRequestCancellation). The comments reference past defects of exactly this class (#318, pool-leak tests).

**Failure scenario.** Any new path that looks a stream up without a lease, or holds one across an await, mutates another request's stream after re-rent: a cross-request state leak that only appears under load. The saving is one ~200-byte object out of roughly ten allocations per request.

## Suggested fix
Measure the allocation gate without the pool; if the difference is one object per request, allocate Http2Stream per request (keeping the embedded value-task source) and delete the lease/identity machinery, or pool the body source and channel instead, where the allocations actually are.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The allocation gate is measured with and without the stream pool and the result is recorded in the PR
- [ ] If the difference is one object per request, Http2Stream is allocated per request and the lease/identity machinery is removed; otherwise the body source and channel are pooled instead
- [ ] Allocations per HTTP/2 request do not increase against the current allocation gate
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [HTTP/2] Comments and docs in the HTTP/2 transport contradict the code or reference vanished review rounds
body:
## Summary
Http2StreamPool.Return documents that PrepareForPool returns a pooled buffer to ArrayPool, although no buffer is held. Http2Settings documents MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS=100 as intended behaviour next to an option that claims to control it, and labels such as 'Fix 3' and 'Fix 8' remain without a referent. A maintainer who trusts these comments builds on behaviour that does not exist.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2StreamPool.cs:42`

## Problem
Http2StreamPool.Return's doc says PrepareForPool 'returns the pooled body buffer (if any) to ArrayPool' (Http2StreamPool.cs:42-44) while the class summary (lines 7-9) and PrepareForPool (Http2Stream.cs:211-244) hold no buffer. Http2Settings.SerializeClientSettings documents 'MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS=100' as intended behaviour next to an option that claims to control it (Http2Settings.cs:98-101). Review-round labels without a referent remain in shipping code: 'Fix 3', 'Fix 8', 'Fix 1', 'Fix 7' (ReadLoop.cs:36, 177, 250, 823) and 'Fix 6' (HpackDecoder.cs:117). 'Backward-compatible constructor' on an internal type (Http2Connection.cs:209, 215). RFC 7540 is cited in public XML docs and type summaries (Http2Options.cs:33, 43, 73, 88; Http2Connection.cs:17; Http2Frame.cs) although the project oracle is RFC 9113. OnStreamChunkConsumedAsync's 'Withdrawn again when the frame was not sent' is false (see http2-design-16). _goawayErrorCode is documented 'guarded by _streamCreateLock' but read outside it through Volatile (Http2Connection.cs:90, Admission.cs:52).

**Failure scenario.** A maintainer trusts the comment (for example that the credit is withdrawn, or that a pooled stream may hold a buffer) and builds on behaviour that is not there.

## Suggested fix
Correct or delete the listed comments; cite RFC 9113 sections in the public docs.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each listed misleading comment is corrected or deleted and review-round labels are removed
- [ ] Public docs cite RFC 9113 sections where they describe protocol behaviour
- [ ] No behaviour change; the shadow build and format checks pass

title: [HTTP/2] About 350 lines of dead or test-only code ship in the Transport assembly
body:
## Summary
PoolableValueTaskSource and its pool, Http2FrameCodec.ReadFrameAsync, HpackDecoder.SetMaxDynamicTableSize with its size-update rule, list-returning Decode overloads and other members have no runtime caller. They are compiled, preserved by link.xml where listed, and maintained, and tests cover code no product path runs. The unused HPACK size-update rule would wrongly require an update after a table-size increase if it were wired up.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http2/PoolableValueTaskSource.cs:56`

## Problem
No runtime caller (rg over Runtime/): PoolableValueTaskSource<T> and PoolableValueTaskSourcePool<T> (PoolableValueTaskSource.cs:56-151, used only by tests); Http2FrameCodec.ReadFrameAsync 'compatibility API' (Http2FrameCodec.cs:88-108); HpackDecoder.SetMaxDynamicTableSize with the _expectingSizeUpdate rule (HpackDecoder.cs:18, 147-151, 182-186; the client never sends HEADER_TABLE_SIZE) and the two list-returning Decode overloads marked [EditorBrowsable] on an internal type (lines 47-66); HpackIntegerCodec.Encode (HpackIntegerCodec.cs:15-34, a second copy of HpackEncoder.EncodeInteger at HpackEncoder.cs:217-236) and the unbounded Decode overload (line 77); HpackHuffman.Encode (HpackHuffman.cs:322-333); Http2ConnectionManager.GetIfExists(host,port), its 4-argument twin and both Remove methods (Http2ConnectionManager.cs:57-64, 83-96, 431-463); the two 'backward-compatible' Http2Connection constructors (Http2Connection.cs:209-219) and the argument-taking Http2Stream constructor (Http2Stream.cs:83-100). Write-only state: Http2Stream.State with Http2StreamState and UpdateStateFromCloseFlags (set at Http2Connection.cs:413 and Http2Stream.cs:190, 230, 540, 586, 825-834, never read, written from several threads without synchronisation), _responseContentLength (Http2Stream.cs:59), HasHandlerFault/_handlerFaulted, Http2Stream.Dispose/IDisposable (never called; the pool uses PrepareForPool), Http2Connection.Host/Port, Http2Settings.MaxConcurrentStreams for local settings, the redundant _localSettings field initialiser and Apply(EnablePush) (Http2Connection.cs:62, 180), and the unused constants MaxFrameSizeMin/MaxFrameSizeMax/MaxWindowSize while Http2Settings.Apply and Http2Options use the literals 16384, 16777215, 2147483647 (Http2Frame.cs:101-104, Http2Settings.cs:65, 72).

**Failure scenario.** The dead members are compiled, kept by link.xml where preserved, and maintained (HpackDecoder's size-update rule would wrongly require an update after a table-size increase if it were ever wired up; State invites a reader to trust a field that is racy and unmaintained). Tests such as PooledValueTaskSourceTests cover code no product path runs.

## Suggested fix
Delete the unused members and move test-only conveniences (ReadFrameAsync, list-returning Decode, Huffman.Encode, short constructors, manager Remove) into the test helpers assembly; use the named protocol constants.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Unused members are deleted and test-only conveniences move to the test helpers assembly
- [ ] The named protocol constants replace the literals that the finding lists

- [ ] Transport assembly size and the Tests/Runtime/Transport/ suite are checked after removal

title: [HTTP/2] SingleReaderChannel never returns its last ArrayPool segment and allocates a Segment object per rented array
body:
## Summary
RentSegment rents a 32-slot array from ArrayPool and wraps it in a new Segment, but only segments passed during Dequeue are returned. The head segment that remains when the channel drains or completes is never returned, so each response that queued a chunk leaks one pool array to the GC. This creates more garbage than a plain small array and the pool bucket never warms up.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http2/SingleReaderChannel.cs:253`

## Problem
RentSegment rents a 32-slot T[] from ArrayPool<T>.Shared, clears it and wraps it in a new Segment (SingleReaderChannel.cs:251-256). ReturnSegment is called only when Dequeue moves to a following segment (232-239); the head segment that remains when the channel is drained or completed is kept (240-246) and neither Complete nor any other member returns it. Each Http2ResponseBodySource owns one channel (Http2ResponseBodySource.cs:64), so every response that ever queued a chunk rents one array that goes to the GC instead of the pool.

**Failure scenario.** Per response with queued DATA the shared pool hands out (and on a miss allocates) a 32-element struct array that never comes back, plus a Segment object: more garbage than a plain small array, and the pool bucket for Http2ResponseBodyChunk[] never warms up.

## Suggested fix
Return the remaining segment when the channel is completed and drained (or give the channel a Dispose called from the body source cleanup), or embed a small fixed inline array for the common one-segment case.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The remaining segment is returned when the channel is completed and drained (or the channel is disposed from the body source cleanup), exactly once on every path
- [ ] Allocations per HTTP/2 response with queued DATA are reduced; the measured count before and after is recorded
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it asserting the segment is returned on complete, cancel and dispose

title: [HTTP/2] Every request in a cold burst dials its own TCP+TLS connection before the HTTP/2 connection is published, and failed redundant dials fail the request
body:
## Summary
RawSocketTransport checks the HTTP/2 manager once and then asks the connection pool, which only bounds concurrency and dials when no idle HTTP/1.1 connection exists. All requests of a cold burst therefore complete a full handshake, and all but one connection is discarded after the manager finds the published one. On mobile with 8 permits, 50 requests need waves of handshakes, and a server that limits connections per client can refuse redundant dials, failing requests although a working HTTP/2 connection exists.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:604`

## Problem
DispatchAttemptAsync checks the manager once (RawSocketTransport.cs:586), then calls _pool.GetConnectionAsync (604). The pool only bounds concurrency with the per-host semaphore and dials when no idle HTTP/1.1 connection exists (TcpConnectionPool.cs:455-530); h2 connections never enter the idle pool and the manager is not re-checked after the permit is granted. Only after the full handshake does GetOrCreateAsync find the published connection and dispose the fresh TLS stream (Http2ConnectionManager.cs:236-241, 313-319). The per-key init lock only deduplicates the HTTP/2 preface, not the dial, despite the class comment ('thundering herd prevention', Http2ConnectionManager.cs:14). If the dial throws, FallBackAfterFailedExtraDial returns null because there is no extra-dial claim (RawSocketTransport.cs:607-611, 1034-1038) and the request fails. No test asserts the number of dials for a cold burst.

**Failure scenario.** App start: 50 requests to one origin are issued at once. On mobile (8 permits) all 50 perform a TCP+TLS handshake in waves of 8; 49 are thrown away. At 100 ms RTT the last requests wait about 2 s for handshakes they do not need, plus 49 certificate validations of CPU and battery. A server or middlebox that limits connections per client refuses some of the redundant dials and those requests fail with a connect error even though the HTTP/2 connection is up.

## Spec reference
RFC 9113 Section 9.1

## Suggested fix
Gate the dial per manager key: the first cold request dials, later requests for the same key await that pending attempt (and re-check the manager after it, and again after the per-host permit is granted); fall back to their own dial only when the first attempt did not yield h2. On a dial failure, re-check the manager before failing the request.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The first cold request for a manager key dials; later requests for the same key await that attempt and re-check the manager afterwards and after the per-host permit is granted
- [ ] Requests fall back to their own dial only when the first attempt did not yield HTTP/2
- [ ] A dial failure re-checks the manager before failing the request
- [ ] 50 concurrent cold requests to one HTTP/2 origin perform one TCP+TLS handshake (measured by a handshake counter)
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it using a loopback HTTP/2 server with a dial counter

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http2-runtime-05` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http2.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: high. Angle: performance.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: DispatchAttemptAsync checks the manager once (RawSocketTransport.cs:586) and then calls _pool.GetConnectionAsync (604). TcpConnectionPool.GetConnectionCoreAsync only takes the per-host permit and, with no idle HTTP/1.1 connection, dials (TcpConnectionPool.cs:461-530); rg finds no HTTP/2 awareness in the pool beyond storing the ALPN result, and the manager is not consulted after the permit is granted. lease.TransferOwnership releases the permit at once (TcpConnectionPool.cs:176-185), so each waiter of a cold burst is admitted, completes a full TCP+TLS handshake, and only then GetOrCreateAsync/GetOrCreateSlowAsync finds the published connection and disposes the fresh stream (Http2ConnectionManager.cs:236-241, 313-319). The init lock deduplicates the preface, not the dial; the extra-dial claim (_extraDials) only covers the saturated-origin case. A failed redundant dial fails the request: FallBackAfterFailedExtraDial returns null when there is no claim (RawSocketTransport.cs:607-611, 1034-1038) and nothing re-checks the manager. The only burst tests are for the saturated extra connection (IdleProbeAndExtraConnections.cs:115, 183). N-1 wasted handshakes for N concurrent first requests to an origin, serialized in waves of MaxConnectionsPerHost; latency, CPU (BouncyCastle on mobile) and server connection-rate limits are all affected.

Also reported as `http2-design-18`, `net-runtime-05` (merged into this issue).

title: [HTTP/2] The ALPN-h2 'hand the stream to the manager and dispatch' sequence is copied four times in RawSocketTransport
body:
## Summary
Direct first dial, direct stale retry, tunnel first dial and tunnel stale retry repeat the same lease transfer, manager call and dispatch steps, and ReleaseExtraDial is called at eight sites. The first-dial copies include the extra-dial fallback and the retry copies do not, and the manager doubles every method for direct and tunnel keys. A lifetime fix applied to one copy is easily missed in the others.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:622`

## Problem
RawSocketTransport.cs:622-644 (direct first dial), 686-696 (direct stale retry), 964-992 (tunnel first dial) and 1133-1150 (tunnel stale retry) repeat RecordEvent / lease.TransferOwnership / _h2Manager.GetOrCreateAsync / null the lease / DispatchOnH2ConnectionAsync; the two first-dial copies add the extra-dial fallback, the two retry copies do not, and ReleaseExtraDial is called at eight sites (lines 640, 646, 743, 988, 994, 1017, 1036 and the fallback helper). The literal "h2" is compared at lines 622, 686 and 1420. Http2ConnectionManager exposes four GetIfExists, two HasConnection, two Remove and two GetOrCreateAsync overloads that differ only in how the key string is built (Http2ConnectionManager.cs:57-110, 161-174, 224-275, 431-463), each formatting a new key string per call.

**Failure scenario.** A lifetime fix made to one copy (ownership transfer after a failed GetOrCreateAsync, claim release ordering) is not applied to the other three; the next key dimension (proxy HTTP/2, #126) doubles the overloads again.

## Suggested fix
Introduce a route-key value (origin, optional proxy) built once per request and one helper 'PromoteLeaseToHttp2AndDispatch(lease, key, ref extraDial, ...)' used by all four sites; collapse the manager overloads onto the key.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A single helper (taking a route key of origin and optional proxy) performs lease promotion and dispatch for all four sites
- [ ] The manager overloads collapse onto the route key and the 'h2' literal is a named constant
- [ ] Behaviour of the direct and tunnel paths is unchanged and the existing HTTP/2 tests pass
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it covering ownership transfer after a failed GetOrCreateAsync on both direct and tunnel paths
